title: Language Movement
subtitle: The protests and killings that made Bangla central to Bengali political identity.
summary: The Language Movement grew out of post-partition inequality, when East Bengal faced cultural and political pressure from a state that privileged Urdu alone. This chapter follows the protests, the police killings of February 1952, and the way language became central to Bengali political identity.
heroTagline: In 1952, the defense of language became a defense of dignity, memory, and political existence.
whyItMatters: The Language Movement explains why Bengali identity, democratic rights, and cultural autonomy became inseparable in East Bengal and later Bangladesh.
culturalImpact: The Language Movement explains why Bengali identity, democratic rights, and cultural autonomy became inseparable in East Bengal and later Bangladesh.
